scope: Prior art, documented primitives and proposed research distinctions; not implementation validation.

sources.title: Blender history
sources.supports: Blender records a community-financed rights buyout followed by GPL release in 2002. This is prior art for buying a proprietary tool into public reuse.
sources.retrieval: Primary organization history; full relevant passage available in web result.

sources.title: Unglue.it Buy-to-Unglue introduction
sources.supports: The 2013 design links sales to earlier open-license release and explicitly discusses buyers waiting near the target. Direct economic prior art for SUNSET.

sources.title: Unglue.it terms
sources.supports: The published terms describe campaign parameters and an initial release date that cannot be moved later. They are evidence of an existing model, not a license template for this project.
sources.retrieval: Relevant full source passages supplied by web search.

sources.title: Functional Source License
sources.supports: A time-based software license conversion precedes SUNSET. The official FAQ describes conversion to MIT or Apache terms after two years.
sources.retrieval: Full page opened and independently fetched with Crawl4AI; expected subject markers present.

sources.title: Purpose Evergreen Capital
sources.supports: The organization describes non-voting investment and capped investor returns. This supports the precedent of finite financial claims, not the proposed contract or any legal equivalence.

sources.title: CollAction
sources.supports: The current organization describes collective activities, participant commitments and crowd actions. Prior art for collective-action products.
sources.retrieval: Full page opened and independently fetched with Crawl4AI; expected subject markers present.

sources.title: Snowdrift mutual assurance
sources.supports: Snowdrift discusses mutual assurance and contributions contingent on others. Conditional collective funding is established prior art.

sources.title: Tabarrok assurance-contract paper
sources.supports: The 1998 paper studies dominant assurance contracts for public goods. It does not validate MOLT or guarantee outcomes outside its model.
sources.retrieval: Author-hosted primary paper; cover, abstract and relevant introductory text retrieved.

sources.title: NEAR access keys
sources.supports: Restricted keys and locked contract accounts are documented. Key gas allowances are distinct from application spending caps, and locked account code can retain authority.

sources.title: NEAR cross-contract calls
sources.supports: External calls are asynchronous and independent; failure does not undo prior receipt state. Atomic formation claims are confined to a single contract execution.

sources.title: OutLayer secrets
sources.supports: The docs describe confidential secrets, exact-WASM binding and owner-controlled access. A revocable creator-owned secret does not prove irreversible public release.
sources.retrieval: Full current official documentation opened; binding and access sections inspected.

sources.title: OutLayer trust and verification
sources.supports: Attested execution, approved measurements and hardware trust are documented. Unattended future disclosure, authentic funding inputs and useful asset quality remain separate questions.

sources.title: drand timelock encryption
sources.supports: Future-round encryption can support a time-based disclosure fallback subject to network assumptions. It does not implement a revenue trigger.
sources.retrieval: Full official documentation opened; old drand.love/docs path returned a general homepage and was not used as the technical reference.

sources.title: Official hackathon agent instructions
sources.supports: Development window, public repository, submission boundaries and conditional track fit. Dates checked on 22 October 2026.

sources.title: Dependency Insurance on NEAR Builders
sources.supports: Existing idea for shared dependency failure response funding. A bounded overlap with migration funding, not evidence of an implemented collective exit service.

sources.title: Verdikt on NEAR Builders
sources.supports: Existing idea uses conditional prediction markets around proposed token fundraising. It is distinct from MOLT but prevents a broad claim that conditional launch decisions are missing from NEAR.
